//: Added 2026-09-15 (audit pass). CI previously gated frontend JS with
`node --check` alone - a pure syntax check that catches an unclosed brace
and nothing else. 7,300 lines of browser JS had no other automated check.
Deliberately narrow, same principle as pyproject.toml's ruff config: only
rules that catch a REAL defect. No stylistic rules at all (no indent,
quotes or semicolon rules) - this codebase already has a consistent house
style, and reformatting 7,300 lines would bury every real finding.
no-undef is deliberately OFF, and that is a considered decision, not an
oversight. This app has no bundler and no ES modules by design (see
CLAUDE.md): all 14 files are plain <script> tags sharing ONE global scope,
so shared.js calling closeModal() (defined in charts.js) is correct code.
ESLint cannot see across files in this arrangement, so no-undef would
either flag hundreds of legitimate cross-file calls, or require an
exhaustive hand-maintained `globals` list - which would itself drift and
become a second source of truth for what every file exports. Neither is
worth it. The rules that remain are all intra-file and fire reliably.
NOTE: this config has not been executed locally - there is no Node in the
development environment it was written in, so the first CI run is what
establishes the baseline. If it reports findings, fix them (or narrow a
rule with a recorded reason); do not silence the step.
